newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's United warns of ACT's "malignant" influence.
newsitem.headline: NZ's United warns of ACT's "malignant" influence.

text.p: The leader of the governing National Party's coalition partner United on Wednesday warned of the danger of an "extremist" right-wing government after the October 12 election.
Clive Matthewson in a statement said he "warned against the danger to New Zealand of an extremist National Government, under the malignant influence of ACT".

Free-market ACT New Zealand is averaging five percent support in recent opinion polls. It has recently ruled out a coalition deal with National but earlier campaigned that a vote for it was a way of ensuring a National government under the new

United is polling less than one percent, but looks set to have at least one MP in parliament after the election. Its Ohariu-Belmont candidate, Internal Affairs Minister Peter Dunne, is well in front in polling in that seat. National chose not to stand a candidate against him.
Matthewson said it was "scary to see the possibility of a National-Act coalition emerging after the election because the result would be a harsh government."
"New Zealanders are not extremists, they do care about their fellow human beings, and they would not like a government guided to the right by blinkered ideologues.

"Lord knows, it's been hard enough for the past six months of the United-National coalition trying to inject a little human warmth into National's uncaring soul. If United's influence were replaced by Act's we'd all be in trouble," Matthewson said.
He also pointed to the left-wing Alliance and economic nationalists New Zealand First as promising the sort of "wildly extreme swings of policy" that he said New Zealand did not want.
United MPs have admitted the party is facing a struggle to differentiate itself from its National coalition partner.
It supports the general thrust of current economic policy but says it wants better, balanced social policies.
